title: Poincare duality and Frobenius similitude
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, and write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; set $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be the
geometric Frobenius acting on the
ordinary cohomology group
$H^i(X,\Ql)$, and let $\langle-,-\rangle_i$ be the
trace–cup-product pairing with values
in the Tate twist $\Ql(-d)$.
The trace map
$\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Ql)\to\Ql(-d)$ is an isomorphism, and for every integer $i$ with
$0\leq i\leq2d$, the pairing
$\langle-,-\rangle_i$ is perfect. Equivalently, it induces a
Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism

$$
H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)
\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Ql)^\vee(-d).
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
$x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$, and every $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, geometric
Frobenius acts on $\Ql(-d)$ by $q^d$, and

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i.
$$

For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
$x\in H^i(X,\Ql)$, and every $y\in H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)$, graded
commutativity gives

$$
\langle y,x\rangle_{2d-i}=(-1)^i\langle x,y\rangle_i;
$$

in middle degree the pairing is $(-1)^d$-symmetric.

proof.text: Identify the maps. In the notation of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], put $V_i=H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $L=\Ql(-d)$. For $0\leq i\leq2d$, the pairing in this statement is precisely $\beta_i(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y)$, with $x\in V_i$ and $y\in V_{2d-i}$. Its trace is the same untwisted trace defined there for the proper structure morphism. Thus every occurrence of trace and pairing below refers to these specified maps.

source.place: Step 1: identification of the specified trace–cup pairing

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-poincare-duality] to the given finite-field datum and $X_0$. Its hypotheses are exactly smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, pure dimension $d\geq0$, and $\ell\ne p$, all assumed here; no exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypothesis is required. Its Trace clause gives the asserted isomorphism $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X:V_{2d}\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, and its Pairing clause gives perfectness of the same $\beta_i$ for each $0\leq i\leq2d$. Explicitly, perfectness says that both induced linear maps to the $L$-valued duals are bijective. In particular $\Phi_i:V_{2d-i}\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(V_i,L)$, $\Phi_i(y)(x)=\beta_i(x,y)$, is a linear isomorphism. Writing this line-valued dual as $V_i^\vee(-d)$ gives the displayed isomorphism as a map of vector spaces; equivariance is checked next.

The Frobenius similitude clause of [thm-weil-poincare-duality] states both that $F_L=q^d\operatorname{id}_L$ and that $\beta_i(F_i x,F_{2d-i}y)=q^d\beta_i(x,y)$, for the geometric Frobenius automorphisms $F_j$ of $V_j$. This is the claimed similitude. On $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ql}(V_i,L)$ the dual-twist action is $\psi\mapsto F_L\circ\psi\circ F_i^{-1}$. For every $x\in V_i$ and $y\in V_{2d-i}$, substituting $F_i^{-1}x$ into the similitude gives
$$
 \Phi_i(F_{2d-i}y)(x)=\beta_i(x,F_{2d-i}y)
 =q^d\beta_i(F_i^{-1}x,y)
 =(F_L\circ\Phi_i(y)\circ F_i^{-1})(x).
$$
Equality for every $x$ proves that the specific isomorphism $\Phi_i$ from step 2 is Frobenius-equivariant, with the required action $q^d(F_i^{-1})^\vee$ on its target.

source.place: Step 3: similitude and equivariance of the pairing-induced isomorphism

proof.text:
Use the graded-commutativity formula in [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup] with degrees $i$ and $2d-i$:
$$
 y\smile x=(-1)^{i(2d-i)}x\smile y.
$$
The difference $i(2d-i)-i=2di-i(i+1)$ is even, since $i(i+1)$ is even. Hence the sign is $(-1)^i$. Applying the linear trace of step 1 gives
$$
 \beta_{2d-i}(y,x)=\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(y\smile x)
 =(-1)^i\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x\smile y)=(-1)^i\beta_i(x,y).
$$
At $i=d$ the two spaces coincide and this is exactly $(-1)^d$-symmetry. This proves the last clause.

source.place: Step 4: graded commutativity and the middle-degree sign
